question.problem: If $\alpha \beta =12$ and $a\cdot b=4$, then what is $(\alpha b)\cdot (\beta a)-21?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the fact that the dot product is linear in both variables, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\alpha b)\cdot (\beta a)-21 & =\alpha (b\cdot \beta a)-21 \\  & =\alpha \beta (b\cdot a)-21.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using that the dot product is symmetric, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha \beta (b\cdot a)-21 & =\alpha \beta (a\cdot b)-21.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $\alpha \beta $ and $a\cdot b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha \beta (a\cdot b)-21 & =12\cdot (4)-21 \\  & =48-21 \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$
